items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The query uses two clearly named CTEs (top_words, top_synsets) with conventional table aliases, consistent indentation and descriptive output aliases. The only blemish is some trailing whitespace after `SELECT `.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The structure is clean: aggregate per word, then rank synsets with ROW_NUMBER, then join. There are no superfluous columns or dead code. The ORDER BY appears twice, but that is needed so LIMIT 500 can be applied early.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: This is a single SQL query with no error-handling surface. The thresholds (>= 2) and LIMIT 500 come from the original query, not from the agent. The agent checked the output with diff before finishing.

items.name: Semantically equivalent, not just equal on this data
items.name_zh: 语义等价而非仅在当前数据上相等
items.evidence: It aggregates `FROM senses s ... GROUP BY s.wordid` and applies LIMIT 500 before `JOIN words w`. That is only equivalent if every senses.wordid exists in words and words.wordid is unique. The schema does not guarantee either; the agent only checked them on this data. Tie-breaks and NULL handling are preserved.
